title: Sin and Death
definition: The doctrine of Sin and Death teaches that death entered the world through sin, showing that rebellion against God is not small, harmless, or merely private.
summary: Sin and Death names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. death entered the world through sin, showing that rebellion against God is not small, harmless, or merely private. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Sin and Death because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: death entered the world through sin, showing that rebellion against God is not small, harmless, or merely private. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because death becomes confusing if it is separated from the fall and from the promise of resurrection in Christ. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Grieve honestly, but not without hope. Let the reality of death make the Gospel urgent and the resurrection of Christ precious. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
